angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 279,705 km at 127.21 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.8611 +/- 0.0360 mas (same row, RUWE 1.04): 127.21 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.402049 +/- 0.031322 solar radii from Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-125 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract): 279,705 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.494727 +/- 0.050755 solar masses from Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-125 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 3654.47 +/- 99.56 K from Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-125 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Dressing et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-125 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....154..207D/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-125.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.924, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
